subject.title: fix(android): keep composer media with its chat

question: Should Android upgrades intentionally fail closed for legacy outbox rows whose original agent owner cannot be proven, requiring manual re-entry or deletion?
rationale: The code can safely prevent cross-owner replay, but choosing user-visible message recovery semantics and accepting the version 4-to-8 stored-data migration requires Android product ownership rather than automated code judgment.

options.title: Approve after upgrade proof
options.body: Accept the fail-closed recovery policy after an exact-head v2026.7.1 database upgrade demonstrates that owned rows remain usable and ambiguous rows remain visible but non-retryable.

options.title: Narrow the change
options.body: Land transient composer ownership first and defer persistent cache/outbox ownership until the upgrade policy is separately approved.

options.title: Redesign legacy recovery
options.body: Pause the PR and define another explicit migration or recovery workflow for ownerless rows before changing the durable schema.

recommendation.title: Approve after upgrade proof
recommendation.body: Accept the fail-closed recovery policy after an exact-head v2026.7.1 database upgrade demonstrates that owned rows remain usable and ambiguous rows remain visible but non-retryable.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the expanded ownership and migration implementation and are the strongest available decision owner for its upgrade semantics.
